say: Before you record, clean the lens. A greasy fingerprint is the most common cause of foggy footage. Check storage and battery, and turn on gridlines to keep things level.
Set 1080p at 30 frames per second. It is sharp enough, with smaller files and less data. Switch on airplane mode so a call does not ruin a good take, and shoot vertical for Reels, Shorts and Status.

panel.heading: Camera setup checklist
items: Lens cleaned with a soft cloth
Storage and battery checked
Gridlines on
1080p at 30 fps
Airplane mode or Do Not Disturb
Vertical 9:16 for Reels and Status

say: Light is the biggest free upgrade. Face a window, with daylight falling on your face. Avoid harsh midday sun and mixed yellow and blue lights.

say: Shaky video is tiring to watch. Hold the phone with both hands and elbows tucked in, or rest it on a tripod or a stack of books. Use the main 1x lens. If you need to be closer, walk closer.

say: For example, Nkechi sells zobo in Owerri. She plans a shot list of wide, medium and close-up shots, each 5 to 10 seconds, so she has room to trim.
She is filming cooking, so the phone and tripod stay away from hot pots and gas flames. And never film while driving or crossing a road.

say: In CapCut, tap New project, add your clips in order, and set the format to 9:16.

panel.heading: Edit in this order
items: Import clips, set format to 9:16
Trim and split; best moment first
Add text and auto captions; proofread
Add music low, so speech stays clear
Export at 1080p, 30 fps

say: Drag the white handles to trim slow starts. Nkechi moved her pouring shot to the start as a 2-second hook, and cut her clips into a 25-second Reel.

say: For example, Joy is a hair stylist in Benin City. Her hook is a close-up of finished braids, with the text, Make your braids last 6 weeks. If people leave in the first 3 seconds, improve the hook.

panel.heading: Script: Hook, Value, Action
items: Hook, 0 to 3 seconds: result or question
Value: one tip, one idea only
Action, last 3 to 5 seconds

say: Her value is three short tips, such as wrapping with a satin scarf at night.

say: About 2 to 3 spoken words per second is a natural pace. Her tip format earned more saves than her photo posts, so she now makes one every Wednesday.

panel.rule: About 60 to 80 spoken words fit a 30-second video.

say: The room matters more than the microphone. Soft things absorb echo, so a bedroom with curtains and a wardrobe of clothes works well. Keep the phone about 15 to 20 cm away, and record a 10-second test first.
Avoid bare rooms, fans and generator noise. Keep voice notes to customers under one minute, and send the price and delivery details as text too.

To remember. Clean lens, good light, steady phone. Plan wide, medium and close-up shots. Put the best moment first and proofread captions. Hook in 3 seconds, one idea, one action. And record sound in a quiet, soft room.

items: Clean lens, good light, steady phone

Quiet, soft room; test before recording
